mainTopic: Health guidance for הקזת דם, and newborn care permitted on שבת (cutting the cord, יחזקאל 16:4)
overview: This amud finishes the גמרא's series of health teachings about הקזת דם (bloodletting) and then returns to the משנה about a newborn on שבת. רב and שמואל teach that one should rest before standing up after bloodletting, and a teaching of מר lists five actions that are dangerous to follow by getting up right away. שמואל then sets the schedule: every thirty days, less often with age, only on certain days of the week, and never on certain dangerous dates such as ערב שבועות. Along the way the גמרא explains Monday and Thursday (days of heavenly judgment), Tuesday (מאדים), and why Friday is still allowed (שומר פתאים ה׳). Next come rules about eating wheat beforehand and about when to drink and eat afterward, including two questions that end in תיקו. A short story about רב's barber prices explains the saying 'a day of mustaches'. The גמרא then returns to the משנה: one may tie a newborn's umbilical cord, רבי יוסי permits cutting it, and the הלכה follows him. Finally, רב derives from יחזקאל 16:4 that delivering, cutting the cord, washing, salting, and swaddling a baby are all permitted on שבת, and פרק מפנין ends.

steps.title: Eating pig after bloodletting causes leprosy
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of a health warning: eating דבר אחר (pig) after bloodletting leads to דבר אחר (צרעת).
steps.simpleTranslation: If one eats 'something else' (pig) after bloodletting, it is harmful and brings on 'something else' (leprosy).
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens in the middle of a list of health warnings about bloodletting. This line finishes one warning: eating pig after bloodletting can bring on צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא uses the polite phrase דבר אחר twice, for two different things. The first refers to pig and the second to צרעת. Both topics are unpleasant, so the גמרא avoids naming them directly.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Something else', a polite way of naming something unpleasant. Here it means pig, and then leprosy.

steps.confusionAlert: The same phrase דבר אחר appears twice in one line with two different meanings. The first means pig and the second means צרעת. They are not the same thing.

phrases.english: [If one eats] 'something else' (pig),
it is harmful, [causing] 'something else' (leprosy).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a bloodletting health warning begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating pig after bloodletting brings on צרעת.

steps.title: Rest a little before standing after bloodletting
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל both teach that after bloodletting a person should wait a bit before getting up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל both said: Someone who has done 'the thing' (bloodletting) should wait a little and only then stand up.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל agree on a practical health rule: after bloodletting, do not jump up right away. Wait a little first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase עביד מילתא ('does the thing') is a short way of saying 'lets blood.' The rule itself is simple. The next step will bring a source explaining why getting up immediately is dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Does the thing', meaning has bloodletting done

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel, who both said:
One who does 'the thing' (bloodletting)
phrases.notes: A polite way of saying bloodletting.

phrases.english: should wait a little and then get up

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new health teaching in the ongoing series on bloodletting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After bloodletting, wait a bit before standing up.

steps.title: Five actions that bring one close to death if followed by standing up immediately
steps.stepSummary: Support from a teaching of מר: five actions followed by standing up right away put a person closer to death than to life, and one of them is bloodletting.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: Five things bring a person closer to death than to life. They are: eating and standing up right away, drinking and standing up, sleeping and standing up, letting blood and standing up, and having marital relations and standing up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רב and שמואל's rule by quoting a known teaching. It lists five activities that are dangerous to follow by getting up immediately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fourth item, הקיז דם ועמד, is exactly the case רב and שמואל spoke about. This shows that their rule is based on an accepted teaching. The other four items show that the body needs a moment to settle after any of these activities.

keyTerms.meaning: As the Master said (introduces a supporting teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: Getting up immediately after eating, drinking, sleeping, bloodletting, or marital relations is considered dangerous, so one should pause first.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
Five things bring one close to death,
more than to life,
and these are they:
one who ate and stood up, one who drank and stood up,
one who slept and stood up,
one who let blood and stood up,
one who had marital relations and stood up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and reason behind רב and שמואל's rule.
steps.raayaObject: רב and שמואל's rule to wait before getting up after bloodletting.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching of מר listing five actions that are dangerous when followed by standing up immediately, including הקיז דם ועמד.

steps.title: Bloodletting every thirty days, less often with age
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the normal interval for bloodletting is every thirty days, and a person should reduce the frequency in middle age and reduce it again in old age.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The interval for bloodletting is every thirty days. In the middle years one should do it less often, and in the later years one should cut back even more.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a schedule for bloodletting. A healthy adult does it once every thirty days, and does it less often as he gets older.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words בין הפרקים refer to stages of life. Each later stage calls for less bloodletting, because an older body is weaker and can tolerate less blood loss.

keyTerms.meaning: The interval or set time for bloodletting

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
The interval for bloodletting
is every thirty days.
And in the middle stages (of life), he should reduce it,
and in the later stages, he should reduce it again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching in the bloodletting series, this time about frequency.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Let blood every thirty days, and reduce the frequency in each later stage of life.

steps.title: Which days of the week are safe for bloodletting
steps.stepSummary: שמואל lists Sunday, Wednesday, and Friday as proper days for bloodletting, and rules out Monday and Thursday.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: The times for bloodletting are Sunday, Wednesday, and Friday. But Monday and Thursday, no.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל tells us which days are good for bloodletting and which days to avoid. The reason for avoiding Monday and Thursday comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The good days are חד בשבתא (Sunday), ארבעה (Wednesday), and מעלי שבתא (Friday). Monday and Thursday are excluded. A question naturally follows: what makes those two days different? The גמרא answers it next.

keyTerms.meaning: The first day of the week (Sunday)

steps.confusionAlert: Here שבתא means 'week', not שבת. So חד בשבתא is Sunday, the first day of the week. Only מעלי שבתא refers to שבת itself, as in Friday, the eve of שבת.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
The times for bloodletting are
the first day of the week, the fourth,
and Shabbos eve;
but the second and fifth days, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from שמואל, moving from how often to let blood to which days to do it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Let blood on Sunday, Wednesday, or Friday, but not on Monday or Thursday.

steps.title: Monday and Thursday are days of heavenly judgment
steps.stepSummary: Support from a teaching of מר: only someone with זכות אבות should let blood on Monday or Thursday, because the heavenly court and the earthly court both sit in judgment on those days.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: Only one who has the merit of his ancestors should let blood on Monday or Thursday, because the court above and the court below are alike.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שמואל ruled out Monday and Thursday. On those days the בית דין של מעלה sits in judgment, so doing something risky then is dangerous unless one has זכות אבות to protect him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earthly courts met on Mondays and Thursdays, and the heavenly court judges on those same days. Bloodletting is a risky act, and doing it on a day of judgment could lead to a harsh outcome. Only someone protected by his ancestors' merit can safely take that risk.
steps.whatToRemember: Bloodletting should be done on Sunday, Wednesday, or Friday. Monday and Thursday are days of judgment both above and below, so they are dangerous for risky acts.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a theme found throughout the גמרא: one should avoid putting oneself in danger at a time of judgment, because exposure to risk invites strict scrutiny from Heaven.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
One who has the merit of his ancestors
may let blood on the second and fifth days,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבֵּית דִּין שֶׁל מַעְלָה וְשֶׁל מַטָּה
phrases.english: because the court above and the court below
are alike (both sit in judgment then).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source and reason for שמואל's exclusion of Monday and Thursday.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that bloodletting should not be done on Monday or Thursday.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching of מר that only one with זכות אבות should let blood on those days, because the heavenly and earthly courts judge at the same time.

steps.title: Why is Tuesday not a day for bloodletting?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why Tuesday was left off שמואל's list of good days for bloodletting.
steps.simpleTranslation: On Tuesday, what is the reason that one does not let blood?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל listed Sunday, Wednesday, and Friday as good days and ruled out Monday and Thursday, but he never mentioned Tuesday. The גמרא asks why Tuesday is not allowed, and the next step will give the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 explained why Monday and Thursday are bad: those are the days of judgment. That reason does not fit Tuesday, so the גמרא needs a separate explanation for why Tuesday is also excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: Tuesday (literally 'the third day of the week')

phrases.english: On the third day of the week (Tuesday),
what is the reason one does not let blood?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the one weekday that שמואל's list in Step 5 did not explain.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason Tuesday is excluded from the permitted bloodletting days.

steps.title: Mars rules the even hours on Tuesday
steps.stepSummary: Tuesday is avoided because the planet מאדים (Mars) rules its even-numbered hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because Mars stands in the even hours on that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: on Tuesday, the planet מאדים controls the even-numbered hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מאדים is linked with blood and violence. Even-numbered hours were also treated as a bad sign. When the two come together on a bloodletting day, that is considered dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: Mars, the red planet, linked with blood

phrases.english: Because there stands (dominant) on it
Mars, in the even hours.
phrases.notes: Each hour was believed to be ruled by one of the seven planets in rotation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Mars dominates the even hours on Tuesday, which makes bloodletting dangerous.

steps.title: But Mars rules the even hours on Friday too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: Mars also rules the even hours on Friday, yet Friday is a permitted day.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ערב שבת, too, Mars stands in the even hours!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem with the answer. Mars also rules the even hours on ערב שבת, and שמואל still allowed bloodletting on Friday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If Mars in the even hours makes Tuesday dangerous, the same reason should make Friday dangerous. Allowing Friday seems to contradict the reason just given for Tuesday.

phrases.english: On Shabbat eve, too, Mars stands in the even hours!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in Step 8 by using שמואל's own permission for Friday in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that Mars in the even hours makes a day forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same planetary situation exists on Friday, yet Friday is permitted.

steps.title: Friday is protected because so many people let blood then
steps.stepSummary: Since the public is already used to letting blood on Friday, ה׳ protects them: 'שומר פתאים ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the multitudes have trodden on it (made it their practice), 'ה׳ protects the simple.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Friday really carries the same risk, but so many people already let blood on Friday that ה׳ protects them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger on Friday is real, so the answer does not deny it. Instead it adds a new principle: when the general public has made a practice of something, the rule of שומר פתאים ה׳ protects them. That is why Friday is allowed even though Tuesday is not.

keyTerms.meaning: The public has trodden on it (it has become common practice)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying Friday is not dangerous. It admits the same risk exists. Friday is allowed only because of the extra protection that comes from common practice.
steps.whyThisMatters: דשו ביה רבים / שומר פתאים ה׳ is a principle used elsewhere in ש״ס to excuse widely accepted practices that carry a small risk.

phrases.english: Since the multitudes have trodden on it (made it common practice),
"The Lord protects the simple-hearted."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא from Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the premise but adds an overriding protective principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The same planetary danger should forbid Friday as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: Friday has the same risk, but common practice brings divine protection, so it is permitted.

steps.title: Four Wednesdays that are dangerous for bloodletting
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that Wednesday is dangerous for bloodletting when it falls on the 4th, 14th, or 24th of the month, or within the last four days of the month.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: a Wednesday that is the 4th, a Wednesday that is the 14th, a Wednesday that is the 24th, and a Wednesday after which there are not four days left in the month are dangerous.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל adds exceptions to his earlier rule. Wednesday is usually a good day, but on certain dates of the month it becomes dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5 Wednesday was a permitted day. Here שמואל narrows that permission: when the fourth day of the week meets a 'four' date (the 4th, 14th, or 24th), or comes near the end of the month, bloodletting is a danger.

keyTerms.meaning: Four, here meaning Wednesday (the fourth day of the week)

steps.confusionAlert: Each 'אַרְבַּע' at the start of a phrase means Wednesday. The number after 'דְּהוּא' is the date of the month.

phrases.english: Shmuel said: the fourth day of the week which is the fourth of the month,
the fourth day of the week which is the fourteenth,
the fourth day of the week which is the twenty-fourth,
the fourth day of the week after which there are not four days left in the month —
is dangerous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from days of the week to dates of the month and limits the Wednesday permission from Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Wednesday that falls on the 4th, 14th, or 24th of the month, or within the last four days of the month, is dangerous for bloodletting.

steps.title: The first three days of the month
steps.stepSummary: Bloodletting on ראש חודש and the second day of the month causes weakness, and on the third day it is dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: ראש חודש and the second day after it bring weakness; the third day brings danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The list of bad dates continues with the beginning of the month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two levels of harm are introduced here. 'חולשא' means weakness, which is a milder harm. 'סכנה' means real danger. The first two days of the month are only weakening, while the third day is actually dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: The New Moon, the first of the month

phrases.english: The New Moon and the second day after it — weakness.
The third day after it — danger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of bad dates for bloodletting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bloodletting on the 1st and 2nd of the month weakens a person; on the 3rd it is dangerous.

steps.title: ערב יום טוב weakens, ערב שבועות endangers
steps.stepSummary: Bloodletting on ערב יום טוב causes weakness, and on ערב שבועות it is dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: ערב יום טוב brings weakness; ערב עצרת (שבועות) brings danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The list moves on to the days before ימים טובים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same two levels of harm appear again. A regular ערב יום טוב only weakens, but ערב שבועות is truly dangerous. This sets up the decree in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: ערב יום טוב, the day before a festival

phrases.english: The eve of a Festival — weakness.
The eve of the festival of Shavuot — danger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of bad dates, using the same weakness/danger levels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bloodletting on ערב יום טוב weakens a person; on ערב שבועות it is dangerous.

steps.title: The decree on every ערב יום טוב because of the spirit טבוח
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן forbade bloodletting on every ערב יום טוב because of שבועות, when a destructive spirit called טבוח comes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן decreed against bloodletting on every ערב יום טוב because of עצרת. On it a spirit named 'טבוח' goes out, for had ישראל not accepted the Torah, it would have slaughtered their flesh and blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the רבנן made a גזירה covering every ערב יום טוב. The reason is the special danger of ערב שבועות and the spirit טבוח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only ערב שבועות is actually dangerous, but the רבנן extended the ban to every ערב יום טוב as a protective fence, likely so that people would not mix up the days. The danger of שבועות comes from טבוח, a destroying spirit that would have killed ישראל had they not accepted the Torah on that day.

keyTerms.meaning: A spirit / wind (here a harmful force)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three kinds of bad dates for bloodletting: certain Wednesdays, the start of the month, and ערב יום טוב. Every ערב יום טוב is forbidden by decree because of the danger of ערב שבועות.

phrases.aramaic: וּגְזַרוּ רַבָּנַן אַכּוּלְּהוּ מַעֲלֵי יוֹמָא טָבָא
phrases.english: And the Sages decreed regarding all Festival eves
because of the festival of Shavuot,
on which a spirit goes out whose name is "Tibbuach,"
for had the Jewish people not accepted the Torah —
it would have slaughtered their flesh and their blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּגְזַרוּ רַבָּנַן אַכּוּלְּהוּ מַעֲלֵי יוֹמָא טָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the danger of ערב שבועות from Step 13 into a rabbinic decree covering every ערב יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bloodletting is forbidden by rabbinic decree on every ערב יום טוב because of the danger of ערב שבועות.

steps.title: Eating wheat before bloodletting cancels it
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that if a person ate wheat and then let blood, the bloodletting only removes the effect of the wheat.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: if one ate wheat and let blood, he only let blood for that wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a new rule about what a person eats before bloodletting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wheat builds up new blood in the body. Whatever blood is let out is simply replaced by the wheat, so the bloodletting does not achieve its goal.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אָכַל חִטָּה וְהִקִּיז דָּם —
phrases.english: Shmuel said: if one ate wheat and let blood —
he only let blood for that wheat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אָכַל חִטָּה וְהִקִּיז דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from when to let blood to what a person eats beforehand.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating wheat before bloodletting makes the bloodletting ineffective.

steps.title: The wheat rule applies only to healing, not to relief
steps.stepSummary: The wheat rule applies only when bloodletting is done to cure an illness; bloodletting done just for relief still works.
steps.simpleTranslation: These words apply to healing, but for relief it does relieve.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits שמואל's wheat rule to one kind of bloodletting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bloodletting can be done for two purposes. If it is meant to cure a sickness, eating wheat beforehand ruins it. If it is only meant to relieve heaviness or discomfort, it still helps even after eating wheat.
steps.whatToRemember: Wheat eaten before bloodletting cancels its healing purpose, but not the relief it brings.

phrases.english: And this applies to bloodletting for a cure,
but to relieve discomfort — it does relieve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of שמואל's rule from Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wheat rule applies only to bloodletting for healing; bloodletting for relief still works.

steps.title: When to drink and eat after bloodletting
steps.stepSummary: After bloodletting, a person should drink right away but should wait the time it takes to walk half a מיל before eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who lets blood should drink immediately. He should wait to eat until the time it takes to walk half a מיל has passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new practical rule: drinking comes right away after bloodletting, and eating comes a little later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a timing rule to the earlier bloodletting advice. Drinking is immediate, while eating is delayed by a set amount of time, measured as the time it takes to walk half a מיל. The next two steps will ask exactly how strict each part of this rule is.

keyTerms.meaning: Half a מיל, a time measure equal to the time it takes to walk that distance

phrases.english: One who lets blood,
drinking: immediately.
Eating: only after the time it takes to walk half a mil.
phrases.notes: Half a מיל is a measure of time, about 9 to 12 minutes according to common opinions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of bloodletting guidelines with a new rule about eating and drinking afterward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drink immediately after bloodletting, and eat only after the time it takes to walk half a מיל.

steps.title: Is drinking later on harmful?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether drinking right away is the only good time, so that drinking later is harmful, or whether drinking later is simply neutral. The question stays unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Drinking immediately is beneficial. Does that mean drinking afterward is harmful? Or perhaps drinking afterward is neither harmful nor beneficial? The question stands unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how to understand the drinking rule from step 17, and no answer is found (תיקו).
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read the rule. In the first, drinking right away helps and drinking later actually hurts. In the second, drinking right away helps and drinking later is simply neutral. The question is left open.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the Sages
Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the rule from step 17 is canceled. Drinking right away is still good. The only open question is the status of drinking later on.

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
drinking immediately is beneficial,
but after that it is harmful,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא לָא קָשֵׁי וְלָא מְעַלֵּי?
phrases.english: or perhaps it is neither harmful nor beneficial?
Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to understand the drinking part of step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether drinking after the immediate window is harmful or only neutral.

steps.title: Is eating before or after the half-מיל point harmful?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether eating is good only at the half-מיל point, so that eating earlier or later is harmful, or whether eating earlier or later is simply neutral. This question also stays unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Eating at the time of half a מיל is what is beneficial. Does that mean eating after that or before that is harmful? Or perhaps it is neither harmful nor beneficial? The question stands unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question about the eating rule, and again there is no answer (תיקו).
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question has two sides. Eating too early and eating too late might both be harmful, or both might simply be neutral. Like the drinking question, it is left open.
steps.whatToRemember: Both questions about the bloodletting food rules end in תיקו. We know when eating and drinking are best, but not whether other times are harmful or just neutral.

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: אֲכִילָה עַד חֲצִי מִיל הוּא דְּקָמְעַלֵּי,
phrases.english: eating at the time of half a mil is what is beneficial,

phrases.aramaic: הָא בָּתַר הָכִי וּמִקַּמֵּי הָכִי — קָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: but after that or before that, it is harmful,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא לָא קָשֵׁי וְלָא מְעַלֵּי?
phrases.english: or perhaps it is neither harmful nor beneficial?
Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: אֲכִילָה עַד חֲצִי מִיל הוּא דְּקָמְעַלֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same kind of question as step 18, now about the eating rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether eating before or after the half-מיל point is harmful or only neutral.

steps.title: רב announces the bloodletter-barber's prices
steps.stepSummary: רב announces that a hundred bloodlettings cost one זוז, a hundred haircuts cost one זוז, and a hundred mustache trims cost nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב would announce: One hundred bloodlettings for a זוז. One hundred haircuts for a זוז. One hundred mustache trims, and nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב makes a public announcement about the prices charged by a bloodletter, who also worked as a barber.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bloodletters also served as barbers. Trimming a mustache was done for free. A day spent only on mustaches would therefore bring in no pay at all. This sets up the next step, where רב יוסף uses this fact to explain a saying.

keyTerms.meaning: Cupping horns used for bloodletting, meaning bloodlettings

phrases.english: Rav would announce:
one hundred bloodlettings for a zuz,
phrases.notes: קרי are the horns used for cupping blood.

phrases.english: one hundred haircuts for a zuz,
one hundred mustache trims for nothing at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from health rules for bloodletting to the bloodletter's pay.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bloodletting and haircuts bring in a little money, but mustache trims bring in nothing.

steps.title: רב יוסף understands the expression 'a day of mustaches'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף recalls that in רב הונא's yeshiva, on lazy days, the scholars would say 'today is a day of mustaches.' He did not understand the saying until he heard רב's announcement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: When we were in רב הונא's yeshiva, on a day when the scholars were lazy in their learning, they would say, 'Today is a day of mustaches.' I did not know what they meant.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tells a memory that the announcement of רב (step 20) now explains for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mustache trim earned nothing, so 'a day of mustaches' means a day with no real gain. Based on רב's announcement, the lazy days in רב הונא's yeshiva were called that because no progress in learning was made on them.

keyTerms.meaning: A day of mustaches, meaning an unproductive day

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a practical fact about a trade explains an expression from the בית מדרש: a day without learning is like a day of work with no pay.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
When we were in Rav Huna's school,
on a day when the Sages were lazy in their study,
they would say: Today is a day of mustaches,
and I did not know what they were saying.
phrases.notes: He means that now, after hearing רב's announcement, he understands it means a day with no gain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: כִּי הֲוֵינַן בֵּי רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב's announcement to explain the meaning of a saying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'A day of mustaches' means an unproductive day, like a barber's day of unpaid mustache trims.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: one may tie the umbilical cord
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה that one may tie the umbilical cord of a baby born on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And one may tie the umbilical cord.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes the next line it wants to discuss. This is a setup line that opens a new topic, and the ברייתא in the next step expands on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא was discussing bloodletting. Now it returns to the משנה's list of things done for a newborn on שבת. The topic here is tying the cord, which is a gentle action done to protect the baby.

phrases.english: And one may tie the umbilical cord.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה to kick off a new discussion about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the bloodletting discussion and returns to the משנה's next line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tying a newborn's umbilical cord is permitted on שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא: tying is allowed, and רבי יוסי allows cutting too
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא repeats that one may tie the cord. רבי יוסי adds that one may even cut it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One may tie the umbilical cord. רבי יוסי says: One may even cut it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches the משנה. It then adds a disagreement: רבי יוסי says cutting the cord is allowed as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the ברייתא (the חכמים) allows only tying. Cutting is a bigger action on שבת. רבי יוסי goes further and permits cutting too, so the two sides argue over cutting, not over tying.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may tie the umbilical cord.
Rabbi Yosei says: One may even cut it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that expands the משנה's line about tying the cord.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים permit tying only. רבי יוסי permits cutting as well.

steps.title: Wrapping the placenta to warm the baby
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: one may wrap up the שליא to keep the baby warm. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל describes what different classes of women wrapped it in.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may cover the placenta so that the baby stays warm. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: princesses cover it in bowls of oil, rich women in wads of wool, and poor women in soft rags.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a second thing that may be done on שבת: wrapping the שליא to warm the newborn. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל then describes how this was done in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People believed that keeping the שליא warm helps keep the baby warm, so it counts as care for the baby. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is not arguing with anyone. He is describing the different materials used, from costly to simple.

keyTerms.meaning: We insulate, cover up to keep warm
Soft rags or scraps of material

phrases.english: And one may cover up the placenta
so that the baby will be warm.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹת מְלָכִים — טוֹמְנוֹת בִּסְפָלִים שֶׁל שֶׁמֶן,
phrases.english: Princesses cover it in bowls of oil,
rich women in wads of wool,
poor women in soft rags.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with another permitted action for the newborn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may wrap up the שליא on שבת to warm the baby. The materials used depend on the family's wealth.

steps.title: רב rules like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב, quoted through a chain of rabbis, rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי: one may even cut the cord.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the argument from the ברייתא. The practical law follows רבי יוסי, so cutting the cord on שבת is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually when one rabbi argues against the majority, the law follows the majority. Here רב rules the other way and sides with רבי יוסי, so cutting is permitted too.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbi in the chain passing down רב's teaching

steps.whatToRemember: Practical law: on שבת one may both tie and cut a newborn's umbilical cord, following רבי יוסי.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said that Rav said:
The law follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument from the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי: one may cut the umbilical cord on שבת.

steps.title: Even the Sages allow cutting a cord that joins twins
steps.stepSummary: רב adds that even the חכמים agree with רבי יוסי when twins are joined by a cord: it may be cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה in the name of רב: The חכמים agree with רבי יוסי about the cord of two babies, that one may cut it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a second ruling. In the case of twins joined by a cord, everyone agrees that cutting is allowed, even the חכמים who normally forbid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows the argument. Even according to the חכמים, there is an exception when two babies are attached. The reason is given in the next steps.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said that Rav said:
The Sages agree with Rabbi Yosei
regarding the cord of two babies,
that one may cut it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling of רב, setting a case where the חכמים also allow cutting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the חכמים permit cutting a cord that joins two babies.

steps.title: Why do the Sages agree here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason the חכמים allow cutting in the case of twins.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the twin case is different. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים normally forbid cutting, so the גמרא needs something special about twins to explain why they change their view here.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the twin case is an exception for the חכמים.

steps.title: Because the twins would pull apart from each other
steps.stepSummary: The twins would pull away from each other and could rip the cord dangerously, so cutting is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they pull apart from each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: if the cord is left, the babies will tug against each other and could tear it, which is dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger to life (פיקוח נפש) is what changes the law for the חכמים. In their view, tying is enough for a single baby. With twins, cutting is needed to keep them safe, so even they permit it.

phrases.english: Because they pull apart from each other.
phrases.notes: They could tear each other's cords

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The joined twins would pull against each other and could tear the cord, which is dangerous.

steps.title: Everything in the rebuke chapter may be done for a woman giving birth
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that every birth-care action mentioned in פרשת תוכחה (יחזקאל 16) may be done on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה in the name of רב: Everything mentioned in the rebuke chapter may be done for a woman giving birth on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a third ruling: a general rule about which newborn-care actions are allowed on שבת. The source verse comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of listing actions one by one, רב points to a passage in נביא. The things the prophet says were not done for the abandoned baby are exactly the things that must be done for every newborn, even on שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'פרשת תוכחה' means יחזקאל 16, not the curses in ויקרא or דברים that are often called by that name.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said that Rav said:
Everything mentioned in the passage of rebuke
may be done for a woman giving birth on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הָאָמוּר בְּפָרָשַׁת תּוֹכָחָה עוֹשִׂין לְחַיָּה בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third ruling of רב, widening the topic from the cord to all newborn care.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All newborn-care actions listed in יחזקאל 16 are permitted on שבת.

steps.title: The verse: cutting, washing, salting, and swaddling
steps.stepSummary: רב supports his rule with יחזקאל 16:4, which lists cutting the navel, washing, salting, and swaddling a newborn.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And as for your birth, on the day you were born, your navel was not cut, you were not washed in water to clean you, you were not salted, and you were not swaddled.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the verse that רב was referring to. It lists four things normally done for a newborn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prophet describes a neglected baby who did not get these four kinds of care. That shows they are the normal, needed care for every baby, so they may be done on שבת. This also matches רב's earlier ruling that cutting the cord is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: For cleansing, to make smooth and clean

steps.whyThisMatters: The verse lists cutting the cord, so it backs up the ruling like רבי יוסי. It also gives a clear list of newborn care that may be done on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: Cutting the cord, washing, salting, and swaddling a newborn are all permitted on שבת, based on יחזקאל 16:4.

phrases.english: As it is stated: 'And as for your birth, on the day you were born,
your navel was not cut,
and you were not washed in water to clean you,
and you were not salted at all,
and you were not swaddled at all.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the verse that supports רב's rule in step 29.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that everything in פרשת תוכחה may be done for a חיה on שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 16:4, listing cutting the navel, washing, salting, and swaddling.

steps.title: The verse teaches delivering the baby and cutting the cord
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the first phrases of the verse. They teach that we may deliver a baby and cut the umbilical cord on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And as for your birth, on the day you were born": from here we learn that we deliver a baby on שבת. "Your navel was not cut": from here we learn that we cut the umbilical cord on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining רב's verse one phrase at a time. Each phrase teaches one action that is allowed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said in general that every action in the verse is allowed. Now the גמרא shows exactly which phrase matches which action. 'On the day you were born' teaches that delivering is allowed, and 'your navel was not cut' teaches that cutting the cord is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: From here we learn. This introduces a lesson taken from a verse.
We deliver a baby. This means helping the birth happen.
Your navel, meaning the umbilical cord

steps.confusionAlert: The verse in יחזקאל is describing a baby who was neglected and did not get this care. The גמרא learns that these are the normal actions done for a newborn, so they are needed even on שבת.

phrases.english: "And as for your birth, on the day you were born"
from here we learn that one delivers the baby on Shabbat.
"Your navel was not cut"
from here we learn that one cuts the umbilical cord on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹלְדוֹתַיִךְ בְּיוֹם הוּלֶּדֶת — מִכָּאן שֶׁמְיַילְּדִים אֶת הַוָּלָד בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks down the verse cited in step 30 into specific lessons
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that the birth-care actions in the verse are allowed on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 16:4, the phrases 'on the day you were born' and 'your navel was not cut'

steps.title: The verse teaches washing, salting, and swaddling the baby
steps.stepSummary: The rest of the verse teaches that we may wash, salt, and swaddle a newborn on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And you were not washed in water for cleansing": from here we learn that we wash a baby on שבת. "And you were not salted": from here we learn that we salt a baby on שבת. "Nor were you swaddled": from here we learn that we wrap a baby on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes going through the verse. It matches the last three phrases to three more actions allowed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing, salting, and swaddling are each linked to their own words in the verse. In the past, people rubbed salt on a newborn's skin to strengthen it. Together with step 31, this completes the list of five actions in רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: For cleansing, to make smooth and clean
We salt. This means rubbing salt on the baby's skin.

steps.whatToRemember: There are five birth-care actions allowed on שבת, all learned from יחזקאל 16:4: delivering, cutting the cord, washing, salting, and swaddling.

phrases.english: "And you were not washed in water for cleansing"
from here we learn that one washes the baby on Shabbat.
"And you were not salted"
from here we learn that one salts the baby on Shabbat.
"Nor were you swaddled"
from here we learn that one swaddles the baby on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְמַיִם לֹא רֻחַצְתְּ לְמִשְׁעִי — מִכָּאן שֶׁרוֹחֲצִין הַוָּלָד בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes the phrase-by-phrase reading begun in step 31
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that the birth-care actions in the verse are allowed on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 16:4, the phrases about washing, salting, and swaddling

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק מפנין
steps.stepSummary: The chapter ends with the traditional farewell formula for פרק מפנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter מפנין.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. It is the closing line that marks the end of the chapter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הדרן עלך' means 'we will return to you.' It shows that we hope to come back and learn this chapter again. The chapter is called מפנין after the first word of its first משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is said at the end of a chapter.
'We clear away.' This is the name of the chapter, taken from its first word.

steps.whatToRemember: פרק מפנין ends with the needs of a woman giving birth and her baby on שבת. Delivering, cutting the cord, washing, salting, and swaddling are all allowed.

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter Mefanin

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the chapter after the final teaching
